answer: First the registry locks a ferrous bond of 0.5 ETH per identity, forfeit on proof of duplicate behavior. Each agent then posts a graded answer; verifier nodes sample it and compare against a rolling consensus, weighting each peer by its own bonded stake. When a grade diverges past tolerance, the divergence is logged on-ledger as a slash trail anyone can replay, and the bond burns on the second strike. Isolated on its own island of stake, a sybil farm cannot subsidize fakes without exposing capital; forging 500 identities costs 250 ETH and a willow-thin 3-day window before consensus collars it.
